A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MemoryAgentBench and contain readable main text and appendices A–L. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection support matching the tables, figures, formulations, and relocated content without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, zero-shot validation, and compute-matched experiments, including Tables 3–5 and 16–19.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results and adds GPT-5-mini benchmark and classification results in Tables 3 and 7.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, incremental memory processing, agent procedures, and prompts remain unchanged. GPT-5-mini is an added comparator; the new hypergraph, reinforcement-learning, and distillation discussions propose future directions without implementing them.

E1.justification: Tables 2 and 6 retain the same datasets and task scenarios across all four competencies. GPT-5-mini is evaluated on existing coverage; no new dataset, domain, or task requirement is introduced.

E2.justification: GPT-5-mini joins the long-context comparators in the overall comparison and five-dataset classification breakdown (Tables 3 and 7). All previous comparators remain, and comparator membership in the other experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added GPT-5-mini evaluation introduces a 400K-token context-window configuration (Table 3 and Appendix C.1). Existing splits, metrics, sample counts, prompts, chunk sizes, and output limits remain unchanged; the new window labels for retained models do not establish changed settings or reruns.

E4.justification: The chunk-size, retrieval-k, backbone, context-length, zero-shot, compute-matched, and overwrite-policy analyses retain their settings and results. The added GPT-5-mini classification breakdown is additional benchmark scoring, not a new ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the reproducibility statement's promise of dataset-generation seeds remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds GPT-5-mini scores, including 60.6 overall and 78.0/28.0 on single-/multi-hop FactConsolidation; Table 7 adds its five classification scores. Section 4.2 consequently updates the Table 3 multi-hop maximum from 7% to 28%. Existing scores are retained, so these are additional comparator results rather than same-model performance gains.

T1.justification: The dataset/agent formulation in Section 3.3 and competency definitions in Appendix B are unchanged. Added connections to other research provide conceptual motivation without new mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the four-competency benchmark, two constructed datasets, unified evaluation framework, and claim that existing agents struggle to master all competencies. The added results do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v4 adds stability–plasticity and collaborative-learning analogies, plus suggested remedies involving temporal hypergraphs, execution-grounded reinforcement learning, and distillation (Appendices B.5, C.2, G, H.1, and I.3). These extend the scientific discussion prospectively; existing limitations and interpretations remain.

D1.justification: Table 3 newly specifies 128K windows for GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini and 200K for Claude-3.7-Sonnet. Appendix C.1 documents GPT-5-mini's 400K window and reasoning capability. Implementation instructions, hardware information, prompts, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds the GPT-5 reference and localized appendix connections to continual/open-world learning, weak supervision and vision surveys, hypergraphs, reinforcement learning, collaborative reasoning, and distillation. The main related-work discussion and benchmark novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Changes comprise localized appendix expansions, the GPT-5-mini description, the numerical finding in Section 4.2, and the arXiv version/date. Most wording and the section sequence remain intact, without extensive rewriting or structural reorganization.

P2.justification: Tables 3 and 7 gain a row; Table 3 adds context-window labels, reorders long-context models, and changes emphasis. Appendix tables reflow, including Tables 14–15 moving from page 27 to 28; figures remain unchanged. EventQA bolding shifts from 82.6 to 78.2 despite the higher retained score.

improvement.justification: Adding GPT-5-mini tests the benchmark's conclusions against another reasoning model at the main evaluation settings, including 28% multi-hop FactConsolidation accuracy, while context-window labels clarify differing input budgets. This provides a modest empirical and transparency benefit. Existing validation is unchanged, the added research directions remain untested, and inconsistent new table highlighting slightly weakens presentation.
